Desk setup

Desk lighting without screen glare

Place a desk lamp around your screen, writing hand and room light, then choose a clamp or base that fits.

Deskwise Guide Editorial · Updated 2 November 2026 · 3 min read
IN THIS GUIDE
  1. Find the reflection first
  2. Compare attachment styles
  3. Useful controls beat feature lists
  4. Watch what the bundle requires
  5. A placement experiment before buying
  6. When a simple lamp wins

Measure first.
Buy with a reason.

Educational buying guide · No hands-on product testing is claimed.

The most useful desk lamp is not necessarily the brightest listing. It is the one that puts light on your task without shining into your eyes or reflecting across the screen. Try moving an existing lamp before deciding that you need a new one.

Find the reflection first

Sit at your usual position with the screen at a normal working angle. Move the lamp and watch for reflections on the display. Then open a notebook and check whether your writing hand casts a shadow over the page. These two observations tell you more about placement than a photograph of someone else's desk.

Compare attachment styles

TypeBest reason to consider itMeasure before ordering
Base lampYou need to move the light frequentlyBase footprint and arm reach
Clamp lampSurface space is scarceClamp opening, frame clearance and top material
Monitor-mounted lightYou want the desktop beneath it clearMonitor shape, mounting limits and webcam position

Useful controls beat feature lists

A reachable brightness control is valuable if you switch between a monitor and paper. An adjustable arm helps when you change tasks. Colour-temperature controls are optional; judge whether the range feels useful in your room rather than treating more modes as automatically better. Check whether controls remember their settings after power is disconnected if you use a switched outlet.

Watch what the bundle requires

Some compact lights use USB power and do not include an adapter. Others have a dedicated mains supply. Verify the power source, cable length and included parts. For cross-border purchases, check the input rating and plug on the supplied adapter; a familiar product name does not guarantee the same regional bundle.

A placement experiment before buying

  1. Clear the proposed mounting point.
  2. Try lighting from either side while writing.
  3. Check the screen with both light and dark content.
  4. Use the setup with your usual room lighting.
  5. Choose only the adjustment range you found necessary.

A monitor light is not a reason to work in a completely dark room, and no lamp can guarantee relief from discomfort. If a lighting change does not solve a persistent problem, do not keep adding brighter accessories as a substitute for appropriate advice.

When a simple lamp wins

A basic lamp with enough reach and a stable base can outperform an elaborate model that cannot mount to your desk. Spend on a fit you can verify. Skip an upgrade if repositioning the current light removes the reflection and leaves the writing area clear.
